subject: URGENT: Customer-reported 5xxs & token latency spikes - Octavian Retail
messages:
From: Octavian Ops <ops@octavian.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 09:12:23 -0700
Subject: High 5xxs & increased tail latency for Redwood API (us-west-2)

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a customer-wide spike in 5xx responses to Redwood API calls from our retail instances in us-west-2 at ~08:45 PDT and it’s persisted in recurring spikes every ~10-15 minutes. Error rate jumps from <0.2% to ~6-8% and median token latency stays fine but p95/p99 rocket to multiple seconds. Attaching a short error log extract and a pcap capture of one failing session.

Key observations from our side:
- Time window: 08:45 - 09:30 PDT (attached logs)
- Most errors are 502/504 coming back through our egress proxy stack, occasionally connection resets.
- We also see DNS resolution latencies spike for redwood-api.redwood.ai from 30ms -> 400ms for a subset of hosts.
- This is affecting checkouts (payment authorization) for several of our stores; we’re seeing revenue impact.

Can you confirm whether there were any changes on your side (peering/egress/firewall/proxy) yesterday or early today? We need an urgent triage call. Sylvia (CTO) is on standby.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Site Reliability Engineer | Octavian Retail
ops@octavian.com

Attachments: octavian_api_500s_snippet.log, egress_trace_pcap_stub.pcap

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: High 5xxs & increased tail latency for Redwood API (us-west-2)

Alex — thanks for the detailed notes and the capture. I’m escalating this to our network and support leads (cc’d). We haven’t deployed any planned peering or firewall changes in us-west-2 in the last 48h, but I want to rule out transient routing or third-party proxy failures.

Immediate plan: 
1) Vanessa/Jonas: run a parallel trace from our us-west-2 egress nodes to Octavian’s collector IPs and validate TLS handshake times and connection pool errors.
2) We’ll enable a short-lived fallback: route a small % of Octavian requests to an alternate egress (us-east-1) to see if the error rate follows.
3) Evelyn: please prepare a customer-friendly update noting we have an escalation with execs and will provide a 30-min bridge option.

Alex, can you confirm if Octavian has any recent changes to NAT gateway scaling, egress proxy TLS termination, or DNS TTLs? If possible, please open a support ticket with your cloud provider for the peering path.

I’m marking this urgent — if we can’t identify a path misconfiguration quickly we will require an exec bridge (Sylvia + our reliability lead).

— Karthik

Subject: Re: High 5xxs & increased tail latency for Redwood API (us-west-2)

On Sat, Apr 14, 2028 at 09:28 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the detailed notes and the capture. I’m escalating this to our network and support leads (cc’d).

I pulled traces from three of our egress hosts in us-west-2 and compared to Octavian’s capture. Preliminary findings: 
- We see repeated TCP retransmits between Redwood egress pool and Octavian NAT IPs coincident with 502/504s. RTT jumps are consistent with an asymmetric route — traffic leaves via one path and returns via a different peering path causing intermittent large buffer/TTL differences.
- DNS: a subset of Octavian’s resolver IPs are returning cached entries with high latency (~300-450ms) before eventually failing over to another resolver. This suggests a resolver upstream with flaky peering rather than internal Redwood DNS.
- Proxy behaviour: we observed connection pool exhaustion on Octavian’s egress proxy. When busy, their proxy returns early 502s rather than queueing upstream.

Immediate mitigations I recommend: 
1) Temporary bypass of Octavian’s egress proxy for Redwood-originating requests (if Octavian can permit us) so clients connect directly and avoid proxy pool exhaustion.
2) Short-lived reroute of ~10% of traffic to our us-east-1 egress to validate whether error-rate and p99 latency improve (we can toggle via routing policy).
3) Octavian netops to check NAT gateway scaling & increase connection tracking timeouts for TLS reuse.

I’ve attached a short pcap snippet (egress_trace_pcap_stub.pcap) and the traceroute output. If Octavian can confirm permission for a direct egress path we can stand up the reroute within ~12 minutes.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Network Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: egress_trace_pcap_stub.pcap

Thanks everyone for the quick triage. Summary and next steps (post-call):
- Impact: intermittent 502/504s and elevated p99 latency for Octavian customers in us-west-2 tied to asymmetric egress path + their egress proxy pool exhaustion. Potential revenue impact; exec attention requested.
- Actions assigned: 
  * Octavian NetOps (Alex / NetOps): scale NAT/egress proxy connection pools and confirm DNS resolver health.
  * Vanessa: implement a 10% reroute to us-east-1 and monitor for error-rate delta (start immediate, rollback if errors rise).
  * Jonas: coordinate customer-facing comms and provide rolling updates to Octavian ops and Sylvia.
  * Rishi: be prepared to open credit/expedited SLA exceptions if impact continues after mitigation window.
- Timeline: reroute & immediate mitigations within 15 minutes of permission; 30-min observation window thereafter. If no improvement, we will escalate to an inter-company network engineering call with Octavian and our backbone provider.

We’ll keep this thread for running notes; Jonas will post a short incident timeline to NET-1543.

— Karthik
